EICMA 2026 • MTPeak Stole Some of the Spotlight at EICMA 2026 With Insane Power and Retro Looks on Three Wheels
Self-Driving Luxury Trailer Pebble Flow Is Faulty, Falling Apart After One Year, Owners Say
87 photos
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing
This could be a case of a bad apple in a good batch or a cautionary tale. Ryan and Celeste, owners of one of the first units of the Pebble Flow produced, are going on the record with their nightmarish first year of ownership and how their unit is falling apart under their very eyes.
Pebble Flow is described by California-based startup Pebble RV as the travel trailer of the future. It's smart in every way imaginable, from the way it parks, hitches, or drives itself, to the way it dumps the black tank or obscures its windows when you want privacy. It's fully electric and with a clean, minimalist design that still makes room for a family of four.
Pebble Flow is, above everything else, a premium product with a price tag to match. Designed for digital nomads or travelers for whom being pioneers weighs heavily in a purchase decision, it starts at around $113,000 before options for the most basic spec.
It will start at that price, better said. Right now, Pebble is delivering the Founders Edition units, which come at prices around $175,000, with volume production scheduled to start once these deliveries wrap.
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing Ryan and Celeste got a Founders Edition Pebble in November 2025, a 2026 unit they paid $190,000. As such, it came with all the bells and whistles that Pebble offers, as well as the "privilege" of being one of the first owners of such a trailer in the U.S.
It wouldn't be long until that privilege turned into a nightmare, as they say in an interview with creator, full-time RV-er, and consumer advocate Liz Amazing. You can see that interview, together with photos that back up their claims, at the bottom of the page.
Everything was good until it wasn't According to the pair, they traveled to California from their home base in Utah to take delivery of their Pebble Flow and were thrilled when the inspection revealed that everything was in order. Ryan, who describes himself as a worker in the solar industry, says the high autonomy of the Pebble Flow was what attracted him to it in the first place.
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing With inspection cleared, the two hitched their Pebble and started the drive back home, and that's when the first issues began. Active Tow Assist, which is the system that helps with towing, stopped functioning on the highway, resulting in strain and drag, and causing stability issues.
The issues continued once they arrived home. They noticed one of the flexible solar panels on the roof had flown off and that the charger stopped functioning with the trailer in storage, locking the system down as the battery drained and leaving them with a techny piece of machinery they no longer had any control over.
Ryan and Celeste never got the chance to go out camping with their trailer, but they did borrow it to his brother for a couple of weeks, and other issues arose. The trailer lost a stabilizer foot on the road, the solar panels became delaminated and stopped working at maximum capacity, and worse yet, it began showing signs of structural degradation.
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing Again, for a trailer they never got the chance to use for its intended purpose, the couple were shocked to see cracks appear in the fiberglass on the corners of the windows and of the door, cracks in weather seals, and the rear emergency escape window became wrapped. Issues also appeared inside, especially in the trim and finishes.
Ryan and Celeste were in contact with Pebble RV from the first signs of trouble and with the technician they sent out in the field to handle the issues. At one point, they were getting contradictory messages: the technician was telling them that the unit would be sent back to the factory for inspection and repairs, while a service manager was saying it wouldn't be, offering the owners retail gift cards instead.
In May this year, the two had had enough of the trailer and formally asked Pebble for a buyback. According to them, it took the company six weeks to finally answer their request, though they still maintained contact – and it was a refusal to take the faulty unit off their hands.
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing "We're afraid to take it out – who knows what's going to fly off next... Owning this has now become a liability," Ryan says. They're not willing to consider keeping the unit, after months of issue and exactly zero use.
Liz says she tried to get a response from the Pebble management, but to no avail. We also reached out but are still waiting for a reply.
Liz's followers flooded Pebble on social media with comments and queries, and one of them finally got a reply. "We're talking to the customer and will make it right," Pebble says.
Photo: YouTube/Liz Amazing The trailer of the future The Pebble Flow debuted in 2023 as a concept and the first Founders Edition units started going out to the first backers in the fall of 2025. Imagined as a trailer of the future, it uses tech and minimalist design to elevate the RV experience while still offering the creature comforts of home.
The trailer measures 25 feet (7.6 meters) in total length and rides on a single axle, offering a cargo carrying capacity of 1,000 lbs (453 kg) and a gross weight of 6,800 lbs (3,084 kg). It comes with two sleeping areas, one at each end and with extra functionality during the day: a U-shaped dinette and a home office, respectively.
Photo: Pebble RV The galley is on the campside, all-electric and with storage in the lower half. Across the way is the full and dry bathroom behind walls of electrochromic glass, the same glass you get all around the trailer .
Everything onboard runs off 1kW of solar on the roof and a 45kWh battery bank. The "brain" of the Pebble Flow is the Nvidia Drive Orin SoC, which offers features like InstaCamp, Magic Hitch, and Auto Dump, allowing you to perform operations (parking, hitching, or dumping the black water) on the Pebble app.
Photo: Pebble RV The travel trailer also comes with Starlink, a four-camera system, and 40 gallons (151 liters) of fresh water, 37 gallons (140 gallons) of gray, and 18 gallons (68 liters) of black water.
Via // Liz Amazing on YouTube
